verdict.summary: HPE’s Q2 FY2026 numbers show that the Juniper combination changed the earnings mix: revenue rose 40% to $10.7B, Networking revenue increased 148.2% to $2.7B and company GAAP gross margin expanded 810 basis points to 36.5%. Cloud and AI revenue of $7.7B still carries only a 12.4% operating margin, so the higher-margin networking contribution is essential to the thesis. The 65/100 fundamental score reflects improving mix but also $21.30B debt, integration risk and Series C mandatory-convertible dilution. The Q2 10-Q reports 30M preferred shares outstanding, up to 87M potentially dilutive common shares and 76M included in diluted shares; this is equity-linked financing, unlike the reviewed straight-debt 424B5. FY2026 free-cash-flow guidance of at least $3.5B provides a measurable deleveraging test. Earnings on September 2 impose an event veto. Wait: $53.96 is a dormant reference absent from the frozen daily and intraday bundles and the event veto remains active; no activation, order or sizing is allowed before a fresh post-earnings RTH structure.

business.overview:
HPE sells enterprise servers, storage, networking, private-cloud systems, software and financial services. Revenue and profit are driven by server unit demand, networking subscriptions and hardware, storage mix, services attachment and financing economics. The Juniper combination materially increased the weight of higher-margin campus, data-center, security and routing products in reported results.

The AI transmission channel spans compute and connectivity. Cloud and AI revenue of $7.7B includes servers and storage that host accelerated workloads, while Networking revenue of $2.7B supplies campus, data-center and routing infrastructure that moves those workloads. NVIDIA demand can pull systems revenue, but networking mix and recurring software are more important to consolidated gross-margin expansion.

What breaks is integration and balance-sheet execution. Juniper customer attrition, delayed synergies, supplier constraints or AI-server pass-through can leave revenue growing faster than profit. Cloud and AI operating margin was 12.4%, well below Networking’s 21.6%. Debt of $21.30B and Series C mandatory-convertible dilution mean the promised $3.5B or greater FY2026 free cash flow must fund deleveraging rather than merely support headline growth.
business.moat: HPE’s moat combines an installed enterprise base, channel reach, support, GreenLake consumption contracts and Juniper’s routing and networking software. The bundle can lower deployment friction, but Cisco, Arista, white-box servers and public cloud keep switching costs from becoming absolute.

capitalStructure.shareHistory: HPE's captured 1.32B common-share count is not presented as a complete basic-to-diluted bridge. The Q2 10-Q reported 30M Series C mandatory-convertible preferred shares, up to 87M potentially dilutive common shares and 76M included in diluted shares; the August dividend adds a $0.953125 cash claim per preferred share. At April 30, $0.933B of debt sat in a bankruptcy-remote financing VIE against $1.606B of financing receivables plus $0.504B of leased equipment. Because HPE does not allocate all corporate borrowings between industrial operations and customer finance, no exact industrial EV is asserted. Final 424B2 accessions establish $2.0B of March 2026 straight debt and a separate $2.9B September 2025 straight-debt offering; neither creates common dilution.

filings.finding: The Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q reports 30M Series C mandatory-convertible preferred shares, up to 87M potentially dilutive common shares and 76M included in diluted shares. It also confirms March issuance of $2.0B straight debt across four series and identifies $0.933B financing-VIE debt against dedicated financing assets.

The FY2025 Form 10-K supplies the audited pre-Juniper baseline for segment margins, debt, customer commitments and capital structure, allowing fiscal 2026 networking growth and leverage to be evaluated without mixing acquisition effects.

The August 4 Form 8-K declares a $0.953125 per-share cash dividend on HPE’s 7.625% Series C mandatory-convertible preferred stock, payable September 1 to August 15 holders; it is a preferred cash claim, not new issuance.

The March 16 Form 424B5 is the preliminary document for the four-series debt offering finalized on March 18. Its blank preliminary economics are superseded by accession 0001140361-26-010157, so it is mapped to that chain once and not counted as separate debt or equity financing.

The final March 18 Form 424B2 prices $2.0B across $300M floating-rate notes due 2028, $500M 4.500% notes due 2028, $600M 4.600% notes due 2029 and $600M 5.250% notes due 2033, with about $1.988B net proceeds. This is straight issuer debt, not equity.

The September 8, 2025 Form 424B5 is the preliminary document for the separate $2.9B four-series offering finalized on September 10. Its blank terms are superseded by accession 0001140361-25-034563, so it is not counted again as another debt or equity transaction.
The final September 10, 2025 Form 424B2 prices a separate $2.9B four-series issuer debt offering. It is straight debt and does not create common-share dilution.
